issue.description: Lock refresh writes to ~/.claude/.credentials.json, or otherwise prove safe coexistence with a concurrently-running Claude Code process writing the same file. §7.1.
issue.notes: Implemented: obtain_access_token() now takes an exclusive OS advisory lock (fs2 flock, bounded retry up to timeout_seconds) on the actual ~/.claude/.credentials.json for the whole read-decide-refresh critical section, serializing against a cooperating concurrent writer (another subgov instance, or Claude Code if it also locks). Because a non-cooperating writer cannot be bound by our lock alone, the refresh result is never written blindly: apply_refreshed_credentials() re-reads the file immediately before the write and compares the refresh token the network call consumed against what is currently on disk. A mismatch means Claude Code (or another process) already rotated it while our HTTP round-trip was in flight; in that case we discard our own refresh and either return the now-current still-fresh access token or fail this poll cycle only -- we never clobber a concurrent legitimate rotation, which would otherwise strand Claude Code on an already-consumed refresh token. Unknown JSON fields in the credentials document are preserved through the CAS write.
issue.title: Lock Anthropic credential refresh writes against Claude Code

Classification: run_cycle's existing Decision/AccountFailure values are mapped by readiness_for_decision/readiness_for_failure -- stale=true -> stale_drain; a window reason of target_reached or banked_resets.manual_redemption_recommended -> intentional_hold (reason 'target_reached'); AccountFailure::Observation -> provider_failure; AccountFailure::Actuation -> actuation_failure; otherwise healthy_learning, with the reason taken from decision.binding_window (added by subgov-ac345750, landed concurrently) resolved back to its WindowDecision.reason.

Installed a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler (ctrlc 3.4) that flips a shared Arc<AtomicBool> instead of terminating immediately. run(): checks the flag after each cycle and after sleeping, exits Ok(()) with a JSONL shutdown event once set. run_cycle() now takes the shutdown flag and checks it before starting each account, so a signal mid-cycle finishes the in-flight account (external observer/actuator calls are synchronous and cannot be interrupted mid-call anyway) and abandons the rest rather than starting new ones; state.save() still runs unconditionally after every cycle so only genuinely-processed accounts advance state.
